title: drogna shell configuration (V2-C19)
description: The shell's configuration document: the views it hosts, the declared component layout the System panel renders greyed-out (structure from declaration, illumination only from received heartbeats — Constitution VII), the topics it reads and the seam endpoints it calls. The shell connects under a role that may read every namespace and may never publish (E13).

role.description: The broker role the shell connects under. Its declaration in the broker's rules must carry an empty publish list.

views.description: The top-level tabs, in first-run order. The view id is the unit of URL addressability (FR-15): '#/view/<id>' opens the shell at that view.

components.description: The declared component layout, rendered from day one, greyed out until each is genuinely heard from. Declaration provides structure and captions only; nothing here can light anything.

beat.description: The narrative beat (feature number) at which this component lands.

all.description: The Messages panel's subscription: everything, because a display may not show cold where there is traffic (E13).

message_schemas.description: Which master governs the messages on each topic, for the client-side validation and refusal counter of E4. A received message whose topic matches no entry is itself counted refused: every crossing has a master or is a finding.

schema.description: The master's stem under contracts/schemas, e.g. 'heartbeat'.

endpoints.description: Relative seam paths the shell calls. Relative and same-origin by requirement (FR-04).

edr.description: The EDR prefix the Map panel and the composer issue genuine GETs against.

features.description: The Features prefix the Map panel reads advisories and reference geometry from.

query_subsets.description: Where the subset statement is served; the composer offers only what it states.

default_window_seconds.description: The window applied to a heartbeat that declares none of its own (heartbeat.schema.json): a tolerance, never a table of components.

buffer.description: How many recent seam messages the Messages panel retains for display.
